metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened delta.com with Round Trip selected by default, proceeded to fill in airports and dates before failing.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can interact with dropdown selectors on delta.com.
metadata.failure_analysis: Delta.com blocked search results. The trip-type change is a single-step action within the reliable prefix.
metadata.task_rationale: Isolate the trip-type dropdown interaction as a standalone task. The agent demonstrated ability to interact with form elements on delta.com. Initial state is 'Round Trip' so a passing evaluator requires switching to 'One way'.
metadata.explanation: Task requires clicking the 'Round Trip' dropdown and selecting 'One way'. Evaluator reads the accessibility tree and checks that 'One way' appears WITH a selection-state indicator (selected/checked) within 50 chars, and that 'Round Trip' is NOT indicated as selected/checked. This prevents false positives from Delta.com rendering all trip-type radio options simultaneously in the tree. [Fixed: renamed getter and metric functions with correct 32-char MD5 hash (45facd29054b2deec3804036a06322c9) replacing invalid 12-char suffix '298e3011319f'] [Fixed: replaced plain substring search with regex requiring selection-state indicator; added negative check that round trip is not selected]

llm_judge_reasons: The metric correctly addresses the previously flagged false-positive issue: it uses regex patterns requiring a selection-state indicator (selected|checked) within 50 chars of 'one way', preventing false positives from unselected radio button labels rendered simultaneously in the accessibility tree.
The negative check correctly verifies that 'round trip' does NOT appear as selected/checked, ensuring the evaluator fails on the initial state where Round Trip is active.

Expected parameter handling is correct: expected.type='rule' means framework passes config['rules'] directly; metric calls expected.get('trip_type', 'One way') and expected.get('exclude_type', 'Round Trip') which are valid direct-access patterns.
No postconfig needed since the trip-type selector is always visible on the Delta homepage — getter can read accessibility tree at any time.
Minor: expected_type variable is extracted but the regex hardcodes 'one.?way' instead of using it. Functionally equivalent (expected_type='One way'), but a slight inconsistency.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: consider using expected_type in the regex instead of hardcoding 'one.?way', for robustness if expected values change (e.g., re.escape(expected_type) in the pattern).
If delta.com's accessibility tree uses 'aria-checked' or 'true' forms instead of 'selected'/'checked' text, the regex may need to be extended to cover those formats.

fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed getter 'get_delta_form_state__298e3011319f' to 'get_delta_form_state__45facd29054b2deec3804036a06322c9' (invalid 12-char MD5 replaced with correct 32-char MD5 computed from 'fc6d8143-9452-4171-9459-7f515143419a|2')
Fix 2: Renamed metric 'check_delta_trip_type__298e3011319f' to 'check_delta_trip_type__45facd29054b2deec3804036a06322c9' (same MD5 fix)
Fix 3: Updated evaluator.func and evaluator.result.type references in JSON to use corrected 32-char hash

Fix 4: Replaced plain case-insensitive substring search ('one way' in tree_text) with regex patterns requiring a selection-state indicator (selected|checked) within 50 chars of 'one way' text, preventing false positives from unselected radio button labels
Fix 5: Added negative check using exclude_type — confirms 'round trip' does NOT appear with a selected/checked indicator in the accessibility tree
